meals.name: Jollof Rice
instructions: Prep: Slice the bell peppers and onions. Mash the garlic with 1 teaspoon salt; seed and slice the Scotch bonnet, and dice the tomatoes.

Build the sauce: Heat sunflower oil in a heavy pot over high heat. Cook peppers and onions, stirring, for 5 minutes. Lower heat to medium; add garlic, Scotch bonnet, tomatoes, thyme, ginger, cayenne, and paprika. Cook, stirring, about 10 minutes, then stir in tomato paste for 1 minute.

Blend and measure: Let the vegetables cool enough to handle. Blend with about 1 1/2 cups stock until smooth. Stir in palm oil and the remaining 1 teaspoon salt. Return 2 1/2 cups sauce to the pot; save any extra. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Cook rice: Stir in the rice until coated. Cover tightly and reduce heat to the lowest setting. Simmer 10 minutes, carefully stir from the bottom, cover and cook 10 minutes more, then stir once more and cook a final 10 minutes.

Steam and serve: Turn off heat and leave covered for 15 minutes. Uncover and rest 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork. If grains remain firm, stir in up to 1/2 cup stock, cover, and cook over low heat for 10 minutes; serve hot.

meals.name: Drunk Apricot Shito
ingredients: ¼ cup dark rum or arrack
3 Tbsp. plus 1 tsp. coconut sugar or dark brown sugar
½ tsp. cubeb pepper or Ashanti pepper (uziza)
½ cup peanut oil or vegetable oil
1 1" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated (unpeeled if organic)
¾ tsp. dried prawn or shrimp powder
1 tsp. okra salt or kosher salt, plus more
1 Scotch bonnet or habanero chile, pierced a few times with a knife
A spice mill or mortar and pestle
instructions: Cover apricots with hot water and soak 20 minutes. Drain, chop, then coat with rum and refrigerate at least 30 minutes (or up to 1 day). Drain over a bowl, reserving both fruit and rum.

Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add cinnamon, 3 tablespoons sugar, and apricots; cook 6-8 minutes, stirring, until softened and coated. Add reserved rum and cook about 5 minutes until syrupy. Set aside.
Toast selim pods and cubeb pepper in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, shaking the pan, about 3 minutes until fragrant. Cool, then crack or grind in a mortar or spice mill.

Warm peanut oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add both onions and cook 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and just beginning to brown. Stir in the ground spices, garlic, ginger, and remaining sugar; cook 5 minutes.

Add pepper flakes, rosemary, thyme, shrimp powder, and salt; stir for 2 minutes. Add apricots and syrup; cook 2 minutes. Stir in tomato puree and cook 4 minutes, then add chile powder, broth, and pierced chile.

Cover and simmer 30-40 minutes, stirring often to prevent sticking, until the sauce is dark and thick and oil rises to the top. Remove the chile if desired, taste and adjust salt, then leave chunky or blend carefully until smooth. Cool completely before transferring to clean jars; cover the surface with a thin layer of oil and refrigerate.

meals.name: Efo Riro with Kale and Whitefish
ingredients: 1 medium onion, quartered through root end
1 red bell pepper, ribs and seeds removed, cut into large pieces
4 skinless tilapia or other whitefish fillets (about 1⅔lb. total), cut into 2" pieces
1 cube Maggi shrimp or chicken bouillon
4 tsp. powdered irú (dawadawa; fermented locust beans)
1 lb. (2 bunches) kale, ribs and stems removed, leaves torn into 2" pieces
Steamed puna yams or rice (for serving)
instructions: Blend the onion, tomatoes, bell pepper, chile, and garlic until smooth, adding up to 1/4 cup water only if needed. Soak bitter leaf in hot water for 10 minutes, drain, and chop.

Season fish with Old Bay. Heat vegetable oil about 1/4 inch deep in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Fry fish in batches, in one layer, turning once, 6-8 minutes total until golden and cooked through; transfer to paper towels. Discard frying oil and wipe out the pot.

Heat olive oil over medium-high. Stir in tomato paste, thyme, garam masala, and turmeric for about 1 minute. Add the blended vegetables, scraping up browned bits, then stir in bitter leaf, shrimp cube, dried shrimp, and iru. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer.

Add kale by handfuls, stirring each addition until it begins to wilt. When all the kale is in, simmer about 5 minutes until tender. Gently fold in fish and heat through without breaking it apart. Serve with yams or rice.

meals.name: Fufu
ingredients: 1 1-lb. small cassava, peeled, woody center removed, cubed
instructions: At least 4 hours ahead (or the night before), freeze the peeled, cored cassava cubes; thaw at room temperature for about 15 minutes before cooking. Peel, cube, and boil the plantains until tender, then drain.

Blend cassava, cooked plantain, and water on high until smooth and as thick as pancake batter. Pour into a heavy pot, stir in salt, and set over medium heat. Stir continuously with a wooden spatula for up to 20 minutes, scraping the bottom and sides, until the dough is smooth and silky.

Wet the spatula and clear away any dough stuck to it. Poke holes through the dough to the bottom of the pot and add 1 teaspoon water to each hole. Cover, lower heat to medium-low, and steam 15-20 minutes until sticky, pliable, and smooth; stir well.
Wet a small bowl and shape portions into smooth balls with damp hands. Serve warm alongside soup or stew.

meals.name: Gbegiri
ingredients: 2 cups dried peeled beans (see note), such as honey beans, black-eyed peas, or peeled mung beans, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the palm oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and cook until translucent, about 4 minutes. Add Scotch bonnet, garlic, ginger, and crayfish; stir until fragrant, about 2 minutes.

Add the peeled, rinsed beans and enough water to cover them by about 2 inches. Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer gently until completely soft and breaking apart; check periodically and add hot water as needed to keep them submerged. Remove from heat and cool slightly.

Blend the bean mixture with about 1 cup water until smooth, working in batches if needed. If using unpeeled beans, pass the puree through a fine strainer. Return soup to the pan and warm over low heat, stirring; add a little water if it is too thick. Serve hot.

meals.name: Ghanaian Fish and Chips (Snapper with Yam Chips)
ingredients: 4 5–6-oz. skin-on red snapper fillets, patted dry
¼ tsp. okra salt or kosher salt, plus more
Alligator pepper or freshly ground black pepper
½ tsp. cubeb pepper or Ashanti pepper (uziza)
½ green or medium-ripe papaya, peeled, insides discarded
1 1" piece ginger, peeled, coarsely chopped (unpeeled if organic)
¼–½ tsp. ground dried bird chiles or other hot chile powder
1 lb. puna, white yams, or sweet potatoes (2–3)
1 tsp. coconut sugar or dark brown sugar
A spice mill or mortar and pestle
instructions: Heat oven to 425°F. Cut the yam or sweet potatoes lengthwise into 1/2-inch wedges. Toss with sugar, 1 teaspoon of the salt, 2 tablespoons olive oil, black pepper, and chile powder. Spread on a baking sheet without crowding and roast 25-35 minutes, turning once, until browned and tender.

Toast the cubeb pepper in a dry skillet over medium-low heat until fragrant, about 2 minutes; grind it. Blend papaya, cilantro, remaining olive oil, red onion, garlic, ginger, ground cubeb, chile powder, and a pinch of salt into a coarse marinade. Coat the snapper and refrigerate for 15-30 minutes.

While the yams roast, heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and lightly oil it. Remove excess marinade from the fish and season with remaining salt and pepper. Grill skin-side down first, 3-4 minutes, then turn and cook 2-4 minutes more, until opaque and it flakes easily. (Alternatively, bake on an oiled tray at 425°F for about 10-12 minutes.)
Serve fish with hot yam chips, lemon halves, and Drunk Apricot Shito.

meals.name: Kunan Aya (Tigernut Milk)
ingredients: ½ Tbsp. whole grains of paradise (atare seeds)
½ cup (50 grams) pitted medjool dates, halved and soaked in warm water
instructions: Toast the ehuru and grains of paradise in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 1-2 minutes, shaking the pan until aromatic. Cool, then grind with ginger, chile, nutmeg, and cinnamon; measure out 1 teaspoon of the blend for this drink.
Rinse tigernuts, cover generously with cool water, and soak at room temperature for at least 12 hours. Drain and rinse again. Drain the soaked dates.

Blend tigernuts, dates, spice blend, and salt with enough fresh water to cover by about 2 inches until very smooth. Work in batches if needed. Pour through a fine-mesh sieve or clean nut-milk bag, pressing firmly to extract the liquid; discard or reserve the pulp.
Chill the milk until cold and stir or shake before serving. Refrigerate and use within 3 days.

meals.name: Mafé Peanut Sauce
ingredients: ½ cup unsweetened creamy peanut butter
¼ tsp. freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium-high. Add onion and cook about 3 minutes, stirring, until softened but not browned. Reduce heat to low; add garlic and tomato paste and cook 3 minutes, stirring often, until the paste darkens slightly.

Whisk in stock and peanut butter until smooth. Add bay leaf, salt, pepper, and cayenne. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and glossy and a little oil rises to the surface.
Remove bay leaf, taste and adjust seasoning, and serve hot over rice, meat, or vegetables. Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 1 week.

meals.name: Market Suya
ingredients: 1 ½ tablespoons roasted peanuts, ground into a ﬁne powder
1 pound jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 pound Wagyu rib eye beef, thinly sliced into strips
1 pound boneless chicken thighs, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Combine cayenne, ground peanuts, paprika, garlic and onion powders, ginger, salt, and crushed bouillon cubes to make the suya spice. Divide shrimp, beef, and chicken among separate bowls; coat each with the spice, cover, and refrigerate for 1 hour.

Heat oven to 400°F. Toss tomatoes with olive oil and a little salt on a rimmed baking sheet; roast 15 minutes and cool. Meanwhile, heat canola oil in a skillet over medium-high. Cook onion 6-8 minutes until soft. Add roasted tomatoes and cook about 10 minutes until broken down. Stir in cream, simmer until thickened, then blend smooth and season to taste.

Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Thread shrimp, beef, and chicken onto separate soaked skewers so each protein can be cooked for its own time. Grill, turning often: shrimp and thin beef strips about 2-3 minutes total; chicken 6-8 minutes total, until the thickest piece reaches 165°F. Serve with tomato-cream sauce.

meals.name: Chicken Peppersoup
ingredients: 2 tablespoons dried bird chiles, or to taste
instructions: Make the spice mix: combine anise, coriander, cumin, allspice, ginger, fennel, Sichuan pepper, tamarind, and cloves. Grind to a fine powder in a spice mill; store extra in a sealed jar.

Rub chicken pieces with lemon juice. Put chicken, water, onion, garlic, chiles, and salt in a large stockpot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a steady simmer and cook 30 minutes, skimming any foam.

Add chicken stock and 1/4 cup spice mix. Simmer about 30 minutes, until chicken is tender and reaches 165°F near the bone. Stir in dried shrimp and mint and cook 10 minutes more. Taste and adjust salt; serve hot with mint sprigs.

meals.name: Egusi Stew
ingredients: 2 cups pumpkin leaf or spinach, strained dry
instructions: Heat palm oil in a large saucepan over medium. Add onion, garlic, tomatoes, ginger, and Scotch bonnet; cook about 10 minutes until softened and translucent. Stir in ground egusi and toast in the oil for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.

Add crayfish powder, bouillon cubes, iru, and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 30 minutes. Meanwhile, season goat with salt and brown on all sides in canola oil over high heat, about 7 minutes total.

Add goat and its juices to the stew. Simmer gently for about 1 hour, partially covered, until the goat is tender and sauce has thickened; stir occasionally and add a little stock or water if it catches. Stir in pumpkin leaf or spinach for the final 20 minutes. Taste, adjust salt, and serve with fufu or pounded yam.

meals.name: Ofe Nsala
ingredients: 1 cup yellow or red Scotch bonnet peppers
¼ cup crayfish, soaked in warm water and drained
1 teaspoon fresh or dried irú, soaked in warm water and drained
15 to 20 large prawns, heads and tails on
4 cups meat, chicken, or vegetable stock
¼ cup rehydrated dried afang leaves
4 cups sliced fresh greens such as mature spinach (optional)
instructions: Make the pepper paste: pound or pulse Scotch bonnets and soaked crayfish to a coarse paste. Add soaked iru and process until smooth. Set aside 1 tablespoon; refrigerate or freeze the rest.

Peel and cube the yam, keeping it in water until ready to cook. Rinse, cover with fresh water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, salt lightly, and simmer 10-12 minutes until completely soft. Drain, cool enough to handle, and mash into small pieces. Devein the prawns while leaving heads and tails attached.

Bring stock to a simmer in a large pot. Add prawns and poach 1-2 minutes, until pink and firm; transfer to a plate. Add pepper paste, dried catfish, and rehydrated afang. Simmer until the stock reduces by about one-quarter. Strain and discard the solids.

Blend 2 cups of the hot stock with mashed yam until smooth, taking care with hot liquid. Return to the pot with remaining stock and stir over low heat until smooth and slightly thickened. Add prawns and optional greens; simmer 4-5 minutes until hot. Season to taste and serve.

meals.name: Puff Puff
instructions: Whisk eggs, granulated sugar, milk, and vanilla in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, whisk flour, salt, baking powder, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Gradually stir dry ingredients into the egg mixture just until a thick, smooth batter forms; rest 10 minutes.
Mix the remaining sugar and cinnamon in a shallow bowl. Pour oil into a heavy pot to a depth of at least 2 inches and heat to 350°F. Keep the oil between 340-360°F as you fry.

Using two spoons, carefully drop tablespoon-size portions of batter into the oil in batches; do not crowd the pot. Fry, turning as needed, for 3-4 minutes until puffed and deep golden and cooked through. Drain on a wire rack or paper towels.
While still warm, toss or dust the fritters with cinnamon sugar. Serve promptly.

meals.name: Roasted Eggplant in Mafé Peanut Sauce
ingredients: ½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper
½ cup crushed roasted peanuts, for serving
2 Tbsp. fresh cilantro leaves, for serving
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F.

Cut off the stem ends of the eggplants, then, using a vegetable peeler or sharp knife, peel vertical strips off of the eggplant skins (like zebra stripes). Cut the peeled eggplants into 1-inch-thick rounds. Place the eggplant rounds on a large sheet pan (overlapping if necessary), brush the rounds with half the oil, and sprinkle half the salt and pepper evenly on top. Flip the rounds and repeat on the other side with the remaining oil, salt, and pepper.

Place the sheet pan in the oven and roast (without flipping) until the eggplant rounds are cooked through and soft but still hold their shape, and the edges are caramelized, about 30 minutes. Transfer the eggplant to a large plate or serving platter and allow it to cool for a few minutes. Generously spoon the warm mafé on each piece, sprinkle with the crushed peanuts and cilantro, and serve.

meals.name: Root Vegetable Mafé
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet or habanero chili, left whole (optional)
1½ cups kosher salt, for blanching vegetables
½ pound peeled and cored fresh or frozen cassava or 1 large peeled russet potato, cut into 2- to 3-inch-thick wedges
2 medium turnips, peeled and cut into 1-inch-thick wedges (about ½ pound)
1 large sweet potato, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes (about ½ pound)
10 medium okra pods, cut into ½-inch slices (optional)
instructions: In a large pot, heat the oil over medium-high heat. Add the onion and garlic, and sauté until soft but not browned, about 5 minutes. Add the tomato paste and reduce the heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently with a wooden spoon, adding a few tablespoons of water as needed to keep the onion and garlic from scorching, until the tomato paste slightly darkens, about 5 minutes.

Add the peanut butter and stir well, using a wooden spoon, to combine. Add the vegetable stock, bay leaf, and Scotch bonnet (if using). Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally to fully dissolve the peanut butter. Season with the sea salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the oil rises to the surface, 15 to 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large pot combine the kosher salt and 1 gallon of water and bring to a boil over high heat. Set a large bowl of ice water alongside. Drop the carrots, cassava, turnips, and sweet potato into the boiling water and blanch until they are just tender but still al dente, about 5 minutes (you may need to work in batches if your pot is not large enough). Using a large slotted spoon, transfer the vegetables to the ice water to stop the cooking, then drain and set them aside.
Add the blanched vegetables and okra (if using) to the peanut sauce and continue cooking until they are soft and easily pierced with a fork, about 10 minutes. Serve with a starch of your choice.

meals.name: Classic French Bouillabaisse With Rouille
ingredients: 1 Turkish or ½ California bay leaf
1 lb. Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled, cut into ½" pieces
⅓ cup finely chopped fennel fronds
1 Tbsp. plus 1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 2¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt
½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper
8 cups Fish Stock or store-bought fish broth
3 lb. white fish fillets (such as monkfish, turbot, red snapper, striped bass, porgy, grouper, and/or cod), cut into 2" pieces
1 lb. cockles or small hard-shelled clams, scrubbed
1 lb. lobster meat, cut into 2" pieces
instructions: Heat oven to 375°F. Arrange baguette slices on a baking sheet and toast 8-10 minutes until crisp. Rub one side of each warm slice with the cut garlic clove and set aside.

Warm 1/2 cup olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add tomatoes, onion, and chopped garlic; cook 5-7 minutes until softened. Add bay leaf, potatoes, fennel fronds, salt, pepper, and saffron. Pour in fish stock, bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer 10-15 minutes until potatoes are nearly tender.

Return broth to a gentle boil. Add the firm fish pieces and cook 3-4 minutes. Add clams or cockles, shrimp, lobster, and mussels; cover and simmer 5-8 minutes, just until fish is opaque and shellfish open. Discard any shellfish that remain closed; avoid overcooking seafood.
Taste the broth and adjust seasoning. Serve the seafood and broth in warm bowls with rouille and garlic toasts.

meals.name: Champagne Chicken
ingredients: ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, plus more
1 large yellow onion, halved through the stem and sliced ¼" thick
12 oz. seedless green grapes, in small clusters on the stem (about 2 ½ cups)
2 tsp. fresh thyme leaves, plus more for serving
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°.
Pat dry one 4-lb. chicken, cut into 8 pieces with a paper towel and season them all over with 1 tsp. kosher salt and ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

In a 12" ovenproof skillet, heat 2 Tbsp. extra virgin olive oil over medium heat. Add half the chicken pieces, skin-side down, and cook undisturbed until the skin is golden brown and the chicken releases fairly easily from the pan, 6 to 8 minutes. (Use a splatter screen if you have one.) Flip and cook until browned on the other side, about 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining pieces of chicken.

Drain and discard all but a thin layer of fat, about ¼ cup, from the skillet. Add 1 large yellow onion, halved through the stem and sliced ¼" thick to the pan along with ½ tsp. kosher salt and a few grinds of pepper. Cook, tossing often, until the onion is lightly browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Add 12 oz. seedless green grapes, in small clusters on the stem (about 2 ½ cups), 4 garlic cloves, minced, and 2 tsp. fresh thyme leaves and cook for 30 seconds, being careful not to let the garlic burn.

Off the heat, add ½ cup Champagne or prosecco and scrape any browned bits from the pan. Return the chicken pieces, skin-side up, along with any accumulated juices to the pan, nestling the larger pieces into the clusters of grapes. Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the breast meat registers 165°, 20 to 25 minutes.

Carefully remove the skillet from the oven and transfer the chicken to a plate to rest while you make the sauce. Add 1 tsp. Dijon mustard to the pan juices in the skillet and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid has slightly reduced. Stir in 2 Tbsp. heavy cream and cook for 1 more minute.

Spoon the sauce onto the bottom of a large serving platter with raised edges. Thinly slice the chicken breast crosswise and arrange on the platter with the rest of the chicken pieces. Scatter the grapes around the chicken. Sprinkle with salt and black pepper, garnish with a few fresh thyme leaves, and serve.

meals.name: Crème Anglaise
ingredients: 1 (2-inch) piece vanilla bean, split; or 1 tsp. vanilla bean paste or extract
instructions: Combine ½ cup whole milk and ½ cup heavy cream in a heavy medium saucepan. Add the scraped seeds and pod from 1 (2-inch) piece vanilla bean, split; or 1 tsp. vanilla bean paste or extract. Bring milk mixture to simmer. Remove from heat.

Meanwhile, whisk 3 large egg yolks, 3 Tbsp. sugar, and a pinch of kosher salt in medium bowl to blend. Gradually whisk hot milk mixture into yolk mixture. Pour mixture back into saucepan and stir over low heat until custard thickens and leaves trail on back of spoon when finger is drawn across, about 5 minutes (do not boil). Strain custard through a fine-mesh sieve into bowl; cover surface directly with plastic wrap or buttered parchment and chill. Do Ahead: Crème Anglaise can be made 1 day ahead; keep chilled.

meals.name: Duck à l'Orange
ingredients: 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt
1 5–6-lb. whole Pekin duck, neck and giblets removed
1 small onion, cut through root end into 8 wedges, divided
½ cup duck or chicken stock or low-sodium chicken broth
Duck or chicken stock or low-sodium chicken broth (if needed)
½ orange, zest removed in wide strips with a vegetable peeler, strips thinly sliced
instructions: Heat oven to 425°F. Mix salt, pepper, coriander, and cumin. Pat duck very dry and prick the skin all over without piercing the meat. Rub the spice mixture over the bird. Place orange, half the onion, and herbs in the cavity; set the remaining onion around the duck in a roasting pan.

Roast breast-side up for 20 minutes. Reduce oven to 350°F, add wine and stock to the pan, and roast about 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, basting occasionally, until the thickest part of the thigh reaches 165°F. Rest 15 minutes before carving; reserve pan drippings.

For the orange sauce, simmer sugar in a small saucepan until it becomes an amber caramel. Carefully stir in orange juice and vinegar; simmer until smooth. Whisk flour and butter together, then whisk into the sauce with orange zest and enough duck or chicken stock to make a pourable sauce. Add strained roasting juices, simmer until lightly thickened, and season to taste.
Carve the duck and serve with the warm orange sauce.

meals.name: Our Favorite French Onion Soup
ingredients: 3 lbs. Vidalia onions (about 4 medium), halved lengthwise, peeled, and thinly sliced
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper, plus more
1½ cups dry white wine such as Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio
6 cups Beef Bone Broth or store-bought low-sodium beef broth
1 garlic clove, cut in half lengthwise
2 tsp. sherry, preferably Fino or Manzanilla, divided
4 oz. (about 1 cup) coarsely grated Gruyère cheese
instructions: In a Dutch oven or other large pot, melt 3 Tbsp. unsalted butter on the stovetop over medium heat. Add 1 Tbsp. vegetable oil and 3 lbs. Vidalia onions (about 4 medium), halved lengthwise, peeled, and thinly sliced, and cook until onions are softened, stirring occasionally, about 15 minutes. Add 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, ½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper, and ½ tsp. granulated sugar. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are deep brown, almost mahogany in color, and caramelized, reducing heat slightly if onions seem to be browning too quickly, 45 minutes to 1 hour more. (If the bottom of your pot begins to burn at any time during the cooking process, add 1–2 Tbsp. water and scrape the bottom, stirring in the browned bits.)
Add 1½ cups dry white wine such as sauvignon blanc or pinot grigio and raise heat to high. Cook until almost all liquid has evaporated, 8–10 minutes.

Tie 10 sprigs fresh thyme and 2 dried bay leaves into a bundle with twine. Add 6 cups Beef Bone Broth or store-bought low-sodium beef stock and herb bundle to pot with onions. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook, uncovered, until broth is thickened and flavorful, 20–30 minutes. Remove from heat and whisk in remaining 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper.

To serve, position a rack in the upper third of the oven and heat the broiler to high. Cut two ½-inch baguette slices for every serving of soup. Place baguette slices on a rimmed baking sheet and toast in oven until crisp and dry but not browned, about 1 minute per side. Rub one side of each toast with the 1 garlic clove, cut in half lengthwise, and set aside.

Place ramekins, crocks, or ovensafe bowls on a rimmed baking sheet, add ½ tsp. sherry, preferably Fino or Manzanilla, to the bottom of each, and ladle soup on top. Top each serving of soup with two garlic-rubbed toasts. Divide 4 oz. (about 1 cup) coarsely grated Gruyère cheese among the servings, covering the toasted bread slices and some of the soup. Carefully transfer baking sheet to oven and broil until cheese is melted and bubbling, 4–8 minutes. (Alternatively, if using regular soup bowls: Top each garlic-rubbed toast with some cheese and return to broiler to melt, about 2 minutes more. Divide sherry and soup among bowls, sprinkle with remaining cheese, and top each serving with two cheese toasts.)

meals.name: Luscious Banana Pudding
ingredients: 2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
1 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
4 ripe (lightly browned in spots) medium bananas, peeled, sliced ½" thick
½ (11-oz.) box Nilla Wafers (about 40 cookies); plus more whole and crushed cookies for topping
instructions: Whisk egg yolks, condensed milk, cornstarch, and bourbon in a heatproof bowl until smooth. In a saucepan, warm milk, 1/2 cup cream, vanilla, and salt over medium heat until steaming but not boiling. Slowly whisk about half the hot milk into the yolk mixture to temper it, then pour everything back into the pan.

Cook over medium-low heat, whisking constantly and reaching into the pan's corners, 5-8 minutes until thick enough to hold whisk tracks. Remove from heat and whisk in butter until melted. Strain if lumpy, cover the surface directly, and chill until cold, at least 2 hours.

Whip 1 cup cream with powdered sugar, vanilla, and a pinch of salt to soft peaks. In a 13-by-9-inch dish, layer wafers, banana slices, and chilled pudding; repeat, finishing with pudding. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours so cookies soften.
Spread or dollop whipped cream over the pudding just before serving. Top with whole or crushed wafers.

meals.name: Cajun Shrimp Pasta
ingredients: 1 lb. homemade or store-bought pasta dough
Grated zest and juice of 1 lemon
½ cup chicken stock or shellfish stock
Kosher salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mix paprika, kosher salt, granulated garlic and onion, black and white pepper, cayenne, thyme, and oregano to make the Creole rub. Set aside what is needed and store the remainder airtight.

Cut pasta dough into four portions. Roll each portion thinly, dusting with flour to prevent sticking, then cut into strands. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook fresh pasta until al dente, usually 2-4 minutes; reserve 1 cup pasta water and drain.

Toss shrimp with 2 tablespoons Creole rub and 2 tablespoons oil. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high; cook shrimp 1-2 minutes per side until opaque, then transfer to a plate. Add remaining oil and butter. Cook onion and both peppers 3-4 minutes until beginning to soften; add garlic, lemon zest and juice, and drained tomatoes, and cook 2-3 minutes.

Stir in cream and stock, season with salt and pepper, and simmer 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened. Mix in Parmesan, shrimp, and pasta; toss over medium heat about 2 minutes, adding a splash of reserved pasta water if needed. Serve hot.

meals.name: Candied Yams
ingredients: 3 lbs. sweet potatoes, such as Garnet yams (about 3–4 large)
1 cup (200 g) packed light brown sugar
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt
instructions: Position a rack in the middle of the oven; preheat oven to 375°F. Peel 3 lbs. sweet potatoes, such as Garnet yams; cut each sweet potato in half crosswise, then cut each piece into quarters so each potato yields 8 large pieces. Transfer to a 3-quart baking dish. Set aside.

Bring ¼ cup water, 1 cup (200 g) packed light brown sugar, 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton Kosher salt, and ⅓ cup bourbon to a simmer on the stovetop in a medium saucepan on medium heat. Cook until sugar is dissolved and syrup has thickened slightly, 3–5 minutes. Pour butter mixture over potatoes.

Roast, basting sweet potatoes every 30 minutes (gently tip casserole dish to one side and spoon sauce on top of the sweet potatoes), until sweet potatoes are fork tender and syrup has thickened into a glaze, 1 hour 30 minutes–1 hour 45 minutes.

meals.name: Chicken Croquettes
ingredients: 3 cups chopped cooked chicken (no skin; a rotisserie bird works well here)
¼ cup minced green bell pepper
½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper
instructions: In a medium bowl, mix together 3 cups chopped cooked chicken (no skin; a rotisserie bird works well here), ½ cup minced celery, ¼ cup minced Vidalia onion, and ¼ cup minced green bell pepper.

In a small bowl, stir together 2 large eggs and 2 Tbsp. heavy cream. Fold it into the chicken and vegetables and season with ½ tsp. kosher salt and ½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper. The mixture will be thick. Form the mixture into 4 round patties 3" across.
In a heavy skillet, melt 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter over medium heat just until foamy. Add the croquettes and cook until golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side. Serve hot.

meals.name: Chocolate Pie
ingredients: 1⅓ cups (161 g) chocolate wafer cookie crumbs
½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
5 oz. fine-quality bittersweet chocolate or semisweet chocolate, melted
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F. Mix cookie crumbs with melted butter and 1/4 cup sugar. Press firmly over the bottom and sides of a pie plate. Bake 8-10 minutes until set, then cool completely.

Whisk 2/3 cup sugar, cornstarch, salt, and egg yolks in a saucepan. Gradually whisk in room-temperature milk until smooth. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, 5-8 minutes until thick and bubbling; continue 1 minute to cook the starch. Remove from heat and stir in both melted chocolates, softened butter, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour filling into the cooled crust. Press plastic wrap directly onto the surface and chill at least 4 hours until firm.
Whip chilled cream with 1 tablespoon sugar to soft peaks. Spoon or pipe over the chilled pie just before slicing.

meals.name: Diner-Style Buttermilk Pancakes
ingredients: 1¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt
½ cup cold seltzer water or club soda
3 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, plus more
instructions: Whisk 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour, 3 Tbsp. sugar, 1¼ tsp. baking powder, 1¼ tsp. baking soda, and 1¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using a fork, beat 2 large eggs, 1¾ cups buttermilk, ½ cup cold seltzer water or club soda, 3 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, and 1 tsp. vanilla extract in a medium bowl to combine. Add egg mixture to dry ingredients and whisk to combine (batter will be slightly lumpy).

Heat a large griddle or 2 cast-iron or nonstick skillets over medium; brush with butter. Working in batches, scoop ½-cupfuls of batter onto griddle; cook pancakes until bubbles form on surface and pop and golden brown underneath, about 3 minutes. Flip and cook until golden brown on other side, about 2 minutes. Transfer pancakes to plates or a platter and brush tops with butter. Serve with pure maple syrup alongside.

meals.name: French Silk Pie
ingredients: 24 Oreo or other creme-stuffed chocolate sandwich cookies
6 oz. bittersweet chocolate, preferably 70% cacao, finely chopped (about 1 cup)
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature
¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt
instructions: Crush cookies to fine crumbs and mix with melted butter. Press evenly over the bottom and up the sides of a 9-inch pie plate. Chill at least 1 hour.

Set a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, making sure it does not touch the water. Whisk eggs and granulated sugar vigorously about 5 minutes until pale and warm. Stir in chopped chocolate, vanilla, and salt until melted and smooth; cool uncovered about 30 minutes.

Beat room-temperature butter with an electric mixer about 3 minutes until fluffy. Beat in cooled chocolate mixture on low just to combine, scrape the bowl, then beat on medium-high about 5 minutes until lighter. In a clean bowl, whip 1 cup cream to stiff peaks and gently fold into the chocolate mixture. Spread in the crust and chill uncovered at least 4 hours.
Before serving, whip remaining cream with powdered sugar, vanilla, and salt to soft peaks. Spread over the pie and finish with chocolate curls if desired.

meals.name: Brochetas de Pescado
ingredients: 1½ lb. tuna or swordfish steaks (about 1½" thick)
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided
½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper
2 chipotle chiles in adobo, seeds removed
5 Tbsp. fresh lime juice, divided (from about 3 medium limes)
4 Tbsp. avocado oil, divided, plus more for grilling
4–6 metal or bamboo skewers (if using bamboo skewers, soak 30 minutes)
instructions: Pat dry 1½ lb. tuna or swordfish steaks (about 1½" thick) and cut into 1½" cubes. Season on all sides with ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton salt and ½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper.

Mince and smash 3 garlic cloves, chopped, and 2 chipotle chiles in adobo, seeds removed, together into a smooth paste. Transfer to a large bowl. Add 1 Tbsp. tomato paste, 2 tsp. ground achiote (annatto seeds), 1 tsp. ground cumin, 3 Tbsp. lime juice, 2 Tbsp. avocado oil, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ⅛ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ¼ cup water and whisk until smooth.
Transfer 2 Tbsp. adobo to a small bowl and whisk in 1 Tbsp. avocado oil and remaining 2 Tbsp. lime juice; set aside.
Transfer fish to large bowl with remaining adobo and toss to coat. Cook immediately or cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate up to 1 hour.
Prepare a grill for medium-high heat or heat a grill pan over medium-high; oil grate. Thread fish cubes onto skewers, 4–5 cubes per skewer.
Grill fish, turning often, until lightly charred, opaque, and firm to the touch, about 2 minutes per side on a grill, and about 2½ minutes per side on grill pan, 8–10 minutes total.
Transfer skewers to a platter. Season with remaining ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ⅛ tsp. Morton kosher salt and drizzle with reserved adobo. Serve with lime wedges alongside.

meals.name: Ceviche Verde With Pepitas
ingredients: ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
1 small red onion, thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
1 lb. skinless fillet mild white fish, such as halibut or sea bass
1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided
½ cup fresh lime juice (from about 5 limes)
⅓ cup lightly packed chopped cilantro, plus whole leaves for serving (optional)
2 Tbsp. mint leaves (from about 2 small sprigs)
½ cup unsalted, roasted pepitas, divided
1¼ cups peeled, seeded, cut into half-moon cucumbers (from about 1 medium English hothouse cucumber or 2 Persian cucumbers)
2 avocados, quartered, sliced lengthwise ¼" thick, divided
instructions: Heat oven to 375°F. Brush tortillas with avocado oil, season with salt on both sides, and bake on a sheet 5-7 minutes. Turn and bake another 5-7 minutes until crisp. Cool on a rack.
Soak sliced red onion in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain. Cut fish into small 1/3-inch cubes, place in a glass or ceramic bowl, and season with half the salt.

Blend serranos, lime juice, chopped cilantro, olive oil, mint, 1/4 cup pepitas, remaining salt, and 2 tablespoons water until creamy, about 2 minutes. Pour over fish and season with black pepper. Add drained onion and cucumber; chill 10-30 minutes, depending on how firm you want the fish.
Fold in remaining pepitas. Arrange avocado on top, add cilantro leaves if using, and serve promptly on the crisp tortillas.

meals.name: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 1¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
½ lb. Monterey Jack cheese, coarsely grated (2½ cups)
Vegetable oil (preferably corn oil, for frying; 2–3 cups)
¼ tsp. kosher salt, divided, plus more
instructions: Char poblanos over a gas flame or under a broiler, turning until blistered all over. Put in a covered bowl 10 minutes to steam, then rub off skins. Make one lengthwise slit in each chile and remove seeds and membranes while keeping stems attached.

Blend tomatoes, onion, garlic, vinegar, sugar, oregano, and salt until smooth. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a saucepan over medium; add sauce and simmer 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Keep warm.

Divide cheese among peppers and close the slits with toothpicks if needed. Separate eggs. Beat whites with 1/8 teaspoon salt to stiff peaks; whisk yolks with remaining salt and fold gently into whites. Heat 2-3 cups frying oil in a deep skillet to 350°F.

Dust stuffed chiles lightly with flour, dip each in egg batter, and fry in batches, turning once, 3-4 minutes total until crisp and golden. Drain on a rack. Serve immediately over warm tomato sauce with rice.

meals.name: Fava Bean Aguachile
ingredients: 9 corn tortillas, each cut into 8 wedges
¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
1 lb. shelled fresh or frozen fava beans
½ cup chopped cilantro, plus whole leaves for serving
⅓ cup fresh lime juice (from about 3 limes)
2 Tbsp. mint leaves (from about 2 small sprigs)
1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided
instructions: Heat oven to 375°F. Toss tortilla wedges with avocado oil and salt; spread in a single layer and bake 5-7 minutes. Turn and bake another 5-7 minutes until crisp. Set aside.

Bring a pot of water to a boil and prepare a bowl of ice water. Boil fresh fava beans 30-60 seconds or frozen beans 2-3 minutes, until bright green and crisp-tender. Drain, chill in ice water, drain again, and peel away any tough outer skins. Place beans in a serving bowl.
Blend serranos, cilantro, lime juice, avocado oil, mint, 1 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons water until smooth, about 2 minutes. Pour over the beans and let stand 15 minutes.
Top with sliced radishes, avocado, and cilantro leaves. Taste and season with remaining salt. Serve with baked totopos.

meals.name: Fideo Seco en Mole
ingredients: About 3 cups chicken or vegetable broth, divided
1 medium avocado, peeled, pitted, and sliced
instructions: Heat the oil in a large, heavy saucepan over high heat. Add the tomato sauce and bring to a boil over high heat. Lower the heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes. Whisk in the mole paste. Whisk in enough of the broth (about 1½ cups) to get you to 4 cups of the sauce. Season to taste with salt, remove from the heat, and set aside. Keep warm.

Heat a large, heavy sauté pan (that will fit both the fideo and the 4 cups of sauce!) over medium heat. Add the fideo and garlic and stir constantly until golden brown. This is done with NO oil! You have to constantly move the fideo, while adjusting the heat, so that it toasts evenly. When it is a light brown color, stir in the mole sauce. Bring to a boil over high heat, lower the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Uncover and stir in 1 cup of the broth (or more if dry). Cover and cook for 5 minutes longer. Adjust the seasoning. Transfer to a platter and serve with crema, avocado, and sesame seeds.

meals.name: Easy Fish Tacos
ingredients: ¼ cup lightly packed fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, plus more for garnish
1 jalapeño, stemmed, seeded if desired, and finely chopped
1 lb. flaky white fish fillets (such as mahi-mahi or cod), cut into 4 pieces
Crema mexicana, fresh salsa, hot sauce, and lime wedges for garnish
instructions: Combine 1 medium red onion, thinly sliced, and 1½ cups red wine vinegar in a small bowl. Set aside for at least 30 minutes.Pour ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil into a shallow medium bowl or dish; add 1½ tsp. ancho chile powder, 1½ tsp. dried oregano, ½ tsp. ground cumin, ¼ cup lightly packed fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, and 1 jalapeño, stemmed and chopped and mix well. Add 1 lb. flaky white fish fillets (such as mahi-mahi or cod), cut into 4 pieces; turn fish to coat well on both sides. Marinate for 20 minutes.

Heat a nonstick sauté pan over medium-high heat. Remove the fish from the marinade and place in the hot pan (no need to add more oil or pat fish dry). Season fish with kosher salt. Cook the fish for 4 minutes undisturbed, then turn over and cook for another 2 minutes. Remove the pan from the heat and flake the fish into the pan with a fork, making sure to mix in all the marinade that has stuck to the bottom of the pan. Check for seasoning and add more salt if necessary. Set aside.

Place 4 of 8 fresh corn tortillas on a plate between 2 slightly dampened sheets of paper towel. Microwave on high for 45 seconds. Place warm tortillas in a towel-lined basket or plate and cover. Repeat with the remaining tortillas.

Spoon a heaping spoonful of cooked fish into the center of a tortilla. Top with pickled onions, crema, fresh salsa, hot sauce, and cilantro leaves. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing. Do Ahead: Pickled onions can be made 3 weeks in advance; refrigerate in an air tight container. Fish can be marinated 1 day ahead; refrigerate in an airtight container.

meals.name: Frijoles de la Olla Ramen (Mexican Stewed Beans)
ingredients: 1 Tbsp. lard or extra-virgin olive oil
⅓ cup (45 g) diced onion (about ⅙ large onion)
1 medium garlic clove, very thinly sliced
¾ cup (110 g) drained canned pinto or black beans
instructions: PRE-SIMMER Heat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add 1 Tbsp. lard or extra-virgin olive oil and ⅓ cup (45 g) diced onion (about ⅙ large onion). Sauté the onion until it has caramelized, about 4 minutes. Add 1 medium garlic clove, very thinly sliced, and sauté for 15 seconds or until fragrant but not browned. Add ¾ cup (110 g) drained canned pinto or black beans, pinch of dried oregano, seasoning sachet from one 3–3½-oz. (85–100 g) packet instant ramen, and 1 cup (240 ml) water.
SIMMER Bring the soup to a simmer. Add the noodle cake and cook for 2 minutes or until your desired doneness.

FINISH Pour the ramen into a bowl. If you’re adding garnishes, top the ramen with chopped cilantro, thinly sliced radishes, cotija cheese, sliced jalapeño, and diced tomato. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

meals.name: Caramelized Plantain Parfait
ingredients: 4 ripe (spotted) plátanos manzanos or 2 large ripe (black) plantains, peeled, sliced in half lengthwise
3 cups plain unsweetened coconut milk yogurt or Greek yogurt
Toasted nuts, seeds, and/or unsweetened shredded coconut (for serving)
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. When shimmering, add plantains in a single layer. Cook about 3 minutes per side, turning once, until deeply golden and tender. Transfer to paper towels and season lightly with salt.
Divide yogurt among serving bowls. Top with warm plantains and sliced mango; finish with toasted nuts, seeds, or coconut as desired.

meals.name: Carne Guisada
ingredients: 1 medium green bell pepper, roughly chopped
1½ pounds boneless pork “country” ribs, cut into bite-size pieces
2 cups water, plus more as needed
½ cup unpitted Manzanilla green olives (optional)
1 Tbsp. salt-free sazón, like Burlap & Barrel Sazón
instructions: Blend tomatoes until smooth. Add onion and garlic and blend, then add bell pepper, cilantro, and optional culantro; pulse until a smooth sofrito forms.

Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high. Pat pork dry, season with salt and pepper, then brown in batches on all sides. Return pork to the pot and add water, 2 tablespoons sofrito, tomato sauce, sazón, and half the olives. Scrape up browned bits, bring to a simmer, then cover partially and cook over low heat about 2 hours until pork is fork-tender; add water if the pot gets dry.

Stir in potatoes and carrots and simmer 10-20 minutes until fork-tender. Mash 2-3 potato pieces against the side of the pot and stir them in to thicken the gravy. Add remaining sofrito and olives, taste and adjust seasoning, and serve with white rice.

meals.name: Dad's Curried Chicken
ingredients: 1 (4-pound) chicken, cut into 8 pieces, skin removed
1 Scotch bonnet pepper or other hot red chili pepper, finely chopped
Roti or white rice, for serving
instructions: Place the chicken pieces in a bowl and toss with the lime juice. Drain, rinse the chicken with cold water, and drain again. Remove the chicken from the bowl and pat dry with paper towels.
Place the chicken in another bowl with the Green Seasoning, salt, chili pepper, and garlic. Toss well to coat and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes but ideally overnight.

Combine the curry powder with just enough water to form a thick paste. Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add the curry paste and onion. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 to 2 minutes over medium-low heat—do not allow the curry to scorch. Add the chicken pieces and stir well to coat. Add the stock or water, cover, and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes, or until the chicken is tender.
Remove the lid and simmer for 5 minutes more over medium-high heat, until the sauce reduces by one-third. Serve with roti or white rice.

meals.name: Djon Djon
ingredients: 6 Maggi brand djon djon bouillon cubes
10 fresh thyme sprigs, tied together with kitchen twine
instructions: Dissolve the djon djon bouillon cubes completely in the hot water in a rice cooker; the liquid will turn dark. Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear and drain well.

Add rice, vegetable oil, sofrito, lima beans, onion, garlic, tied thyme, Scotch bonnet, and salt to the cooker. Stir to distribute, then close the lid and run the steam/rice cycle (about 30 minutes, or follow the cooker's instructions).
When the cycle ends, let the rice stand covered for 5 minutes. Remove the thyme and whole chile if desired, fluff gently, taste for salt, and serve.

meals.name: Grilled Jerk Tofu and Plantains With Mango Salsa
ingredients: 4–6 Scotch bonnet or habanero chiles, seeds removed, or 1–2 tsp. Scotch bonnet chile powder
16–20 allspice berries or 2 Tbsp. ground allspice
1 Tbsp. plus 1 tsp. browning sauce (preferably Grace; optional)
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
¼ cup avocado oil or vegetable oil
1 Scotch bonnet chile or jalapeño, seeds removed
⅔ cup coarsely chopped red bell pepper
½ cup coarsely chopped red onion
½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
¼ cup avocado oil or vegetable oil, plus more for grill
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
4 very ripe (almost black) plantains, halved lengthwise
Thinly sliced scallions and lime wedges (for serving)
instructions: Press tofu between towels under a weighted plate for 20-30 minutes to remove excess moisture. Blend red onions, scallions, garlic, chiles, thyme, ginger, allspice, soy sauce, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup vinegar, lime juice, optional browning sauce, pepper, 2 teaspoons salt, nutmeg, cinnamon, and 1/4 cup oil into a thick jerk marinade.

Cut tofu into thick slabs and coat thoroughly with marinade. Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour, preferably up to overnight. Blend lime juice, chile, mango, bell pepper, red onion, cilantro, and optional agave or honey into a chunky salsa; season with the listed salt and chill.

For the plantains, whisk the 2/3 cup brown sugar and 1/4 cup vinegar with the plantain salt and pepper. Brush plantains with oil, then coat with the mixture. Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and oil the grate. Grill tofu 4-6 minutes per side until marked and hot throughout. Grill plantains cut-side down, turning once, about 3-4 minutes per side until caramelized and tender. Serve with salsa, scallions, and lime wedges.

meals.name: Hummingbird Cake
ingredients: 1⁄4 cup coconut oil, at room temperature
1⁄2 cup (113 grams) sour cream, at room temperature
2 cups (454 grams) mashed very ripe bananas, about 5
1 cup (114 grams) chopped pecans or pecan pieces
1½ pounds (681 grams) cream cheese, at room temperature
3⁄4 cup (185 grams) unsalted butter, at room temperature
instructions: Make the cake. Preheat the oven to 325°F. Lightly coat two 9-inch round cake pans with 4-inch-high sides with baking spray, then line the bottoms of the pans with parchment paper and lightly spray the paper. (If you don’t have 4-inch-deep pans, 2-inch-deep will work.)

In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking soda, cinnamon, rose petals, and cardamom and mix well. In a medium bowl, lightly whisk the eggs with the vegetable oil, coconut oil, vanilla, and salt, then stir in the dry ingredients, mixing just until they are moistened. Stir in the sour cream. Using a large spatula, fold in the crushed pineapple and juice, bananas, and pecans. Divide the batter evenly between the prepared pans. Bake the cakes in the center of the oven for about 45 minutes, rotating the pans after 20 minutes, until the cakes are golden brown and a cake tester or toothpick comes out clean when inserted into the center of each cake. Let the cakes cool in the pans on a wire rack for 15 to 20 minutes. Place a rack over each pan, invert the cakes onto the racks, and remove the pans. Peel off the parchment paper. Cool completely.

Make the frosting. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment or in a large bowl using a handheld mixer, beat the cream cheese and butter on medium-high speed until smooth. Sift the powdered sugar into the bowl; beat until incorporated and smooth. Stop the mixer and scrape down the bottom and sides of the bowl with a rubber spatula to ensure that the frosting is as smooth as possible. Beat in the orange zest and vanilla paste.

Using a serrated knife, trim the domed tops of the cakes so they’re flat; save the scraps for snacking. Cut each cake horizontally into two even layers, creating four layers in total. Set one layer on a cake stand or plate and spread with the frosting. Continue to stack and frost the layers, then spread a thin layer of frosting all over the cake.

Refrigerate for 15 minutes, until set. Spread the remaining frosting evenly all over the sides and top of the cake. The cake will keep at room temperature for about 4 days, if it ever actually sticks around that long.

meals.name: Mofongo
ingredients: 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt
2 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 Tbsp. plus ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
4 medium green plantains, peeled, sliced crosswise 1" thick
Cilantro leaves and lime wedges (for serving)
instructions: Cut pork belly into thick strips. Combine with the first measure of salt, pepper, oregano, cumin, paprika, lime juice, and orange juice in a heavy pot. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce heat and cook uncovered, turning occasionally, until the liquid evaporates and the pork fat renders, about 45-60 minutes.

Continue cooking the belly in its rendered fat, turning as needed, until the skin is deep golden and crisp, about 8-12 minutes. Transfer to a rack and cut into bite-size chicharrones. Keep the rendered fat in the pot.

Dissolve the remaining salt in a bowl of water and soak plantain slices 10 minutes; drain and dry thoroughly. Heat frying oil to 350°F. Fry plantains in batches 5-7 minutes until golden and tender; drain and season with some of the measured salt.

Pound garlic with olive oil in a mortar. Add hot plantains in batches and mash to a coarse mixture, leaving texture; fold in some chicharrones. Shape into compact mounds while warm and serve with remaining pork, cilantro, and lime wedges.

meals.name: BeaverTails
instructions: In the bowl of a stand mixer, add warm water, a big pinch of sugar and yeast. Allow to sit until frothy.
Into the same bowl, add 1/2 cup sugar, warm milk, melted butter, eggs and salt, and whisk until combined.
Place a dough hook on the mixer, add the flour with the machine on, until a smooth but slightly sticky dough forms.
Place dough in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and allow to proof for 1 1/2 hours.
Cut dough into 12 pieces, and roll out into long oval-like shapes about 1/4 inch thick that resemble a beaver’s tail.
In a large, deep pot, heat oil to 350 degrees. Gently place beavertail dough into hot oil and cook for 30 to 45 seconds on each side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels, and garnish as desired. Toss in cinnamon sugar, in white sugar with a squeeze of lemon, or with a generous slathering of Nutella and a handful of toasted almonds. Enjoy!

meals.name: Breakfast Potatoes
instructions: For easier dicing, chill or briefly freeze the bacon until firm but not frozen solid. Wash potatoes, cut into even medium dice, and hold in cold water while you prepare the remaining ingredients.

Heat 1-2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Drain and dry the potatoes thoroughly, add to the hot pan in an even layer, and season with salt, pepper, and Old Bay. Cook about 10 minutes, turning frequently, until browned and nearly tender; add a little more oil if the pan becomes dry.

Add chopped bacon and cook 5-6 minutes, stirring, until browned and crisp and the potatoes are tender. Lower heat to medium-low, stir in garlic, and cook about 1 minute until fragrant. Add parsley and adjust seasoning.
Drizzle in maple syrup and toss for about 1 minute until lightly glossy and caramelized. Serve hot, with a sunny-side-up egg if desired.

meals.name: Canadian Butter Tarts
instructions: Preheat the oven to fan 170C/ conventional 190C/gas 5. Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface so it’s slightly thinner than straight from the pack. Then cut out 18-20 rounds with a 7.5cm fluted cutter, re-rolling the trimmings. Use the rounds to line two deep 12-hole tart tins (not muffin tins). If you only have a regular-sized, 12-hole tart tin you will be able to make a few more slight…

Beat the eggs in a large bowl and combine with the rest of the ingredients except the walnuts. Tip this mixture into a pan and stir continuously for 3-4 minutes until the butter melts, and the mixture bubbles and starts to thicken. It should be thick enough to coat the back of a wooden spoon. Don’t overcook, and be sure to stir all the time as the mixture can easily burn. Remove from the heat and …

Spoon the filling into the unbaked tart shells so it’s level with the pastry. Bake for 15-18 minutes until set and pale golden. Leave in the tin to cool for a few minutes before lifting out on to a wire rack. Serve warm or cold.

meals.name: Classic Tourtière
ingredients: 1 tsp Dried Leaves Of Summer Savoury
instructions: Heat oil on medium-high heat in a large sauté pan or skillet, then sauté the onion and garlic until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the ground beef, pork, and spices and cook until the meat is browned.

Add the beef broth and bring it up to a simmer then reduce heat to medium low. Add the grated potato and stir it in. Cook until liquid is almost absorbed, about 15 min. Remove the bay leaves and add salt to taste. Remove the pan from the heat and let the mixture cool completely — it bakes best if the filling is chilled.

Preheat the oven to 375 °F (190 °C). On a lightly floured surface, roll out one disc of the pie dough to less than the 1/4-inch thickness and line the 9-inch pie plate. Fill this with the cooled tourtière mixture and spread out evenly. Roll out the remaining dough to the same thickness, cut a hole in the centre (for steam to escape) and place on top of the filling. Trim the dough to 1/2-inch beyon…
Bake tourtière for about 45 minutes or until the pastry is a rich golden brown. Let cool for 15 minutes before slicing to serve.
Serves: 8-10 (makes 2 9-inch pies)

meals.name: Date squares
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Grease an 8-inch (20 cm) square baking pan.

To make the date filing: Combine the dates and water in a medium saucepan over high heat and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer gently, stirring occasionally until the mixture thickens, around 6 to 8 minutes. Remove from heat, stir in vanilla and let cool. Set aside.

Combine rolled oats, flour, sugar, baking soda and salt in a food processor. Pulse 3 times (careful not to overmix, you don’t want the mixture to be powdery, just combined). Add butter and pulse again until the mixture is crumbly in pea-sized clumps. Transfer to a mixing bowl to thoroughly mix in the butter.

Spread half of the oat mixture on the bottom of the prepared baking pan, pressing down to make a flat, equal bottom later. Add the date mixture over the crust and then spread evenly. Layer with the remaining oat mixture and press down to flatten the top layer.

Bake in the centre of the oven until the top is golden brown, 30 to 35 minutes. Let cool completely in the pan before cutting and serving. Date Squares keep well, covered in the refrigerator for up to a week, and frozen for 2 to 3 months.

meals.name: Figgy Duff
instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, brown sugar, baking powder, and spices.
Add raisins and stir well, making sure to coat the raisins in the flour mixture.

Add melted butter, molasses and water and mix with a wooden spoon. Form a ball with the spoon or your hands and put the dough ball in a cotton pudding bag. Tie the bag, leaving at least 1 inch of room to allow the pudding to expand while cooking.
Boil pudding for 1.5 hours. (In NL, this is typically done in the pot along with Jiggs Dinner, but it can be done independently.)
When the duff is firm, remove it from the boiling water and let it cool slightly before removing it from the pudding bag.

Slice pudding like a cake and serve with the warm sauce of your choice: rum butter sauce, warmed molasses or Molasses Coady sauce (1 cup (250 mL) molasses, 1/4 cup (60 mL) butter, 1/4 cup (60 mL) water) is common in Newfoundland.

meals.name: Braised Beef Chilli
instructions: Preheat the oven to 120C/225F/gas mark 1.

Take the meat out of the fridge to de-chill. Pulse the onions and garlic in a food processor until finely chopped. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large casserole and sear the meat on all sides until golden.

Set to one side and add another small slug of oil to brown the chorizo. Remove and add the onion and garlic, spices, herbs and chillies then cook until soft in the chorizo oil. Season with salt and pepper and add the vinegar, tomatoes, ketchup and sugar.
Put all the meat back into the pot with 400ml water (or red wine if you prefer), bring up to a simmer and cook, covered, in the low oven.
After 2 hours, check the meat and add the beans. Cook for a further hour and just before serving, pull the meat apart with a pair of forks.

meals.name: Cajun spiced fish tacos
instructions: Pat fish dry. Combine Cajun spice, cayenne, and a little seasoning on a plate, then press the fish into the mixture to coat all sides. Mix the dressing ingredients in a small bowl and season to taste.

Heat a thin film of oil in a skillet over medium. Cook fish in batches without crowding, turning once, until golden and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes total depending on thickness (145°F at the thickest point). Transfer to a plate and break into large flakes.
Warm tortillas briefly in a dry skillet or microwave until pliable. Fill with avocado, lettuce, spring onion, salsa, and fish. Drizzle with dressing and serve.

meals.name: Chicken Enchilada Casserole
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into large pieces and place in a saucepan with the enchilada sauce. Cover and simmer over low to medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, about 20 minutes or until the chicken reaches 165°F. Lift chicken out, reserve the sauce, and shred with two forks.

Heat oven to 375°F. Spread about 1/4 cup reserved sauce over the base of a baking dish. Layer tortillas, one-third of the chicken, sauce, and cheese; repeat twice, finishing with tortillas, remaining chicken, sauce, and cheese.
Bake uncovered 20-30 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is melted and lightly browned. Rest 5 minutes before serving warm.

meals.name: Chickpea Fajitas
instructions: Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6 and line a baking tray with foil. Drain the chickpeas, pat dry and tip onto the prepared baking tray. Add the oil and paprika, toss to coat, then roast for 20-25 mins until browned and crisp, shaking halfway through cooking.

Meanwhile, put the tomatoes and onion in a small bowl with the vinegar and set aside to pickle. Put the avocado in another bowl and mash with a fork, leaving some larger chunks. Stir in the lime juice and season well. Mix the soured cream with the harissa and set aside until ready to serve.
Heat a griddle pan until nearly smoking. Add the tortillas , one at a time, charring each side until hot with griddle lines.

Put everything on the table and build the fajitas : spread a little of the harissa cream over the tortilla, top with roasted chickpeas, guacamole, pickled salsa and coriander, if you like. Serve with the lime wedges for squeezing over.

meals.name: Crock Pot Chicken Baked Tacos
instructions: Put chicken breasts in a slow cooker. Pour the full bottle of dressing over them, add the listed seasonings, and turn the chicken to coat. Cover and cook on HIGH for about 4 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F and shreds easily.

Transfer chicken to a plate and cool briefly. Shred with two forks, then moisten with most of the slow-cooker liquid. Stir avocado and green salsa together and strain if a smooth drizzle is desired. Thin sour cream with milk until pourable.
Heat oven to 450 F. Fill taco shells with refried beans, shredded chicken, and cheese; stand them in a 9-by-13-inch baking dish. Bake 10-15 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbling.
Top with tomatoes, jalapeno, and cilantro. Drizzle with avocado salsa and sour cream sauce; serve hot.

meals.name: Stuffed Bell Peppers with Quinoa and Black Beans
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish or a similar-sized casserole dish.
Place the bell pepper halves in the prepared baking dish, cut side up. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until slightly softened.

While the bell peppers are baking, prepare the filling. In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, and cook for 3-4 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic, and cook for another 1 minute, until fragrant.

Stir in the cooked quinoa, black beans, corn, diced tomatoes, ground cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until heated through. Remove the skillet from heat, and stir in 1 cup of the shredded cheese, if using.
Remove the bell peppers from the oven, and carefully stuff each pepper half with the quinoa and black bean mixture. Top the stuffed peppers with the remaining 1/2 cup of shredded cheese, if using.
Return the stuffed peppers to the oven, and bake for another 15-20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the peppers are tender.
Remove from the oven, and allow the stuffed peppers to cool for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.

meals.name: Brown Stew Chicken
instructions: Squeeze lime over chicken and rub well. Drain off excess lime juice.
Combine tomato, scallion, onion, garlic, pepper, thyme, pimento and soy sauce in a large bowl with the chicken pieces. Cover and marinate at least one hour.
Heat oil in a dutch pot or large saucepan. Shake off the seasonings as you remove each piece of chicken from the marinade. Reserve the marinade for sauce.
Lightly brown the chicken a few pieces at a time in very hot oil. Place browned chicken pieces on a plate to rest while you brown the remaining pieces.
Drain off excess oil and return the chicken to the pan. Pour the marinade over the chicken and add the carrots. Stir and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Mix flour and coconut milk and add to stew, stirring constantly. Turn heat down to minimum and cook another 20 minutes or until tender.

meals.name: Callaloo and SaltFish
instructions: Soak salted fish in plenty of cold water overnight in the refrigerator. Drain, cover with fresh water in a saucepan, and bring to a boil. Drain as soon as the water boils, cool, remove bones and skin, and flake the fish.

Cook bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp. Transfer bacon to a plate and pour off all but about 1 tablespoon fat. Add yellow and green onions, Scotch bonnet, and garlic; cook about 2 minutes until softened. Stir in flaked fish and cook 1 minute.

Add callaloo, tomatoes, thyme, and black pepper. Toss until greens wilt and everything is hot, about 5-8 minutes. Taste before adding salt because the fish may remain salty. Top with crisp bacon and serve.

meals.name: Escovitch Fish
instructions: Pat fish dry and rub with citrus juice, salt, and pepper or the listed seasoning. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Fry fish in batches, about 5-7 minutes per side depending on thickness, until crisp and cooked through; transfer to a warm plate. Leave 2-3 tablespoons oil in the pan.

Add bay leaf, garlic, and ginger and stir about 1 minute, taking care not to brown the garlic. Add onion, bell peppers, thyme, Scotch bonnet, sugar, and allspice; cook 2-3 minutes until beginning to soften. Pour in vinegar, stir, and simmer 2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Remove bay leaf and thyme. Spoon the hot escovitch vegetables and vinegar over the fish. Serve with bammy or the listed accompaniment.

meals.name: Callaloo Jamaican Style
instructions: Separate kale leaves and tender stems from tough stems. Rinse well and soak in cold water 5-10 minutes, then drain and cut into bite-size pieces. Slice onion, mince garlic, and dice tomato and red pepper.
Cook bacon in a saucepan over medium heat until crisp. Add onion, garlic, and thyme; cook about 2 minutes until fragrant. Stir in tomato, red pepper, and paprika; cook 2-3 minutes.
Add kale and a small splash of water, cover, and steam 6-8 minutes, stirring once, until tender. Season to taste and keep warm.

Peel bananas and cut lengthwise into medium slices. Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium. Cook slices in a single layer, turning and adding a little oil as needed, until browned and tender on both sides. Season lightly and serve with the callaloo.

meals.name: Caribbean Tamarind balls
instructions: Add tamarind pulp and 1 cup granulated sugar to a bowl and mash together with a spoon or fork. Take small amounts of the tamarind and sugar mix and shape them into small balls by rolling them in your hands. Make them the size of a marble or slightly bigger, as you like.
Add the remaining sugar to a flat surface, like a plate or a sheet pan. Roll the tamarind balls in granulated sugar until they're well-coated.
You can eat the tamarind balls immediately, or you can let them set for a few hours or overnight. Allowing them to set will give them a firmer texture and more crystallized sugar coating. Enjoy.

meals.name: Corned Beef and Cabbage – Jamaican Style
instructions: Heat olive oil in a skillet or Dutch pot over medium-high. Add onion and green pepper and cook 3-5 minutes until softened. Stir in garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add shredded cabbage and cook 3-5 minutes, stirring often, until it begins to soften. Add corned beef, tomatoes, thyme, ketchup, and Scotch bonnet sauce; break up the beef and stir to combine.
Lower heat to medium and cook 3-5 minutes until the beef is hot throughout and the flavors come together. Taste before adding salt, then serve with rice or bread.
